pills.text: OLD NCERT ITSELF ENDS BY CALLING INDUSTRIALISATION A SOURCE
THEREFORE THE PHRASE "MIXED BLESSING" IS ENTIRELY LEGITIMATE WHEN
OLD NCERT EXPLICITLY CONNECTS INDUSTRIALISATION WITH THE SEARCH FOR
IT ALSO NOTES THAT INDUSTRIAL COUNTRIES SUBORDINATED THE ECONOMIES
THIS IS THE CORRECT BRIDGE TO LATE-19TH-CENTURY IMPERIALISM

groups.heading: OPTIONAL SOURCE DEPTH
items: Old NCERT itself ends by calling industrialisation a source of both benefits and hardships / evils .
CAUTION: Therefore the phrase "mixed blessing" is entirely legitimate when supported with evidence.
Old NCERT explicitly connects industrialisation with the search for markets , raw materials , and eventually imperial expansion .
It also notes that industrial countries subordinated the economies of weaker regions to their own interests.

groups.heading: ADVANCED DEBATE
items: CAUTION: This is the correct bridge to late-19th-century imperialism: industry did not
mechanically create empire, but it greatly intensified the pressure for empire .
CAUTION: For India-specific consequences such as deindustrialisation, drain and colonial market
subordination, cross-link rather than repeat: Modern-Indian-History/basic/07 Economic-Impact-of-British-Rule.md and Modern-Indian-History/advanced/07 Economic-Impact-of-British-Rule.md.

groups.heading: LEGACY / NUANCE
items: Enclosure movement, colonies, coal, iron, shipping and capital formation are central to the English lead.
Early labour reform included Factory Acts and the eventual legalisation of trade unions.
Laissez-faire is associated with the early capitalist belief in minimum state interference.
Industrialisation strengthened the pressure for tariff policy, market protection and imperial competition.
